(sam with Skt. abhi˚), makes a profound bow: ger. ˚ṇamya (taṃ mahākapiṃ; but here, and always, the acc. could also be construed with the main verb, and the ger. regarded as without complement);;; ˚ṇaman (n. sg. m. pres. pple.).
(sam plus abhiprasīdati, Skt. ˚sādayati), makes completely well-disposed: ppp. ˚sādita;.

, ppp. (= AMg. ˚bhūa,; no sam-abhi-bhū- in Skt. or Pali; sam- with Skt. and Pali abhibhūta in mg. 1), (1) conquered:; surpassed, outdone,; (2) (overwhelmed? and so) overspread, covered (with light, prabhayā):.
(cf. Skt. abhiv˚), accepts with respect (a command or request): (mātur vacanaṃ kusumamālām) iva śirasā ˚vandya (ger.) ….

(sam with abhyud˚), arises, comes forth: teṣv (sc. buddhakṣetreṣu) ayaṃ mamātmabhāvavigrahastūpaḥ ˚gacchet; (cakraṃ … tasya mūrdhnaḥ) ˚gamya (ger.) … bhramitum ārabdham.
(cf. Skt. ˚peya, subst. nt., in different mg.), approaches: (dharmarājāḥ …) iha madanugrahaṇāt ˚paintu (vs; metr. correct; ˚pa-yantu would be unmetr.).

, (1) time, as in Skt.; app. nt. (Skt. only m.) in, see s.v. ardharātri; tena samayena (as in Pali), at that time, very common in phrase introducing a new episode, tena khalu punaḥ samayena (Pali tena kho pana sa˚), now, however, at that time …,;;;;, etc. (in many passages, incl. some of these, a voc. intervenes between punaḥ and sam˚); (2) (Pali id.; not in Skt., not even in Vedic; is to be taken otherwise, see) assembly, congregation, concourse (of persons), = Skt. samiti: punar api devasamaye yadā satyāṃ prakāśayet = (vs); a rare usage, here and seemingly in Pali; (3) nt., a high number:, cited in as samarya, q.v.; the corresp. form in seems to be sāmpa (prob. corrupt).
(denom. from Skt. sama), see sameti.

, adj. (= Pali ˚vimutta), released temporarily, occasionally, from time to time: (opp. to asamaya-vimukta, q.v.). Pali also has nouns (a)samaya-vimutti, ˚vimo(k)kha. See (§§ 1, 2); (on). There are eight states of ‘temporary release’, viz. the four dhyāna (or rūpāvacara-samāpatti), the four arūp(āvacar)asamāpatti (so). See also. (mistranslates the Pali.)

(acc. to, eine Verabredung habend, and m. ‘eine Art Mönch’), possibly doing what the occasion (samaya) requires: kulejanmānunmādī samayī hevajradeśakaḥ (vs). But I suspect a corruption; the meter is śloka, and as it stands, the first syllable of this word belongs to the first pāda, the rest of it to the second! I do not recall any parallel to this.

(or, with v.l., śama˚), having even splendor, or (śama˚) the splendor of tranquillity, ep. of the Bodhisattva Dīpaṃkara = (repeated of Śākyamuni); also, in same context,, instead of amara-ruci (metr. inferior).

acc. to, ‘wohl Zusammenbiegen, Krümmen, von sam-ṛj’; he then suggests that Pali saṃmiñjeti (our saṃmiñjayati, q.v.) stands for *sam-riñjayati for sam-ṛñjayati, which I think unlikely: in fragment 44 V 1 () of : ārabhate śarīraṃ saṃtāpana (lacuna) … aṅgāvapāṭana-samarjana-vṛ(tt) … (lacuna). The mg. seems to be quite different from that of saṃmiñjana, ˚jita, qq.v.; here we seem to have to do with a form of (self-?)torture.

, or samajji˚, mss., em. saṃmarji˚; none of these forms conveys a mg. to me; I suggest samarcitaka, one that has been treated with respect, well-treated (ppp. of Skt. sam-arc- plus -ka): (Yaśodharā is [Page566-a] dissuading Rāhula from monastic life) tvaṃ … sukhocito rājakule saṃvṛddho tvaṃ ca putra ˚tako vīṇāvaṃśapaṇavamadhurāṃ śabdāṃ śruṇamāno kathaṃ te ratir bhaviṣyati (in ascetic life) (prose).

, adj.-ppp. (not in this mg. in Skt., but = Pali samappita), affected, filled (with feelings, pleasant or unpleasant, in comp.): te sukha-˚tā bhaviṣyanti; kṣutpipāsā- (mss. always ˚sa)-˚tānāṃ, ˚tāni; well provided, ˚to kāmaguṇehi pañcabhiḥ.
, m., or nt. id., a high number; in cited from which reads samaya, nt., q.v. (3).

(nt. or m., in Pali id., nt., wrongly given as ˚lā, f., in; cf. Vedic, also, śamala, and Skt. Lex. sa˚), filth, or sewer (cf. samalaṃ nāma gūtha-niddhamana-panāḷi): nāstitā-dṛṣṭi-samale yasmād asmin nimajjati.
, ppp. (of sam- with Skt. avag˚; = AMg. samogāḍha), plunged, entered (into water): te … lavaṇajaladharaṃ ˚gāḍhā(ḥ).
= Pali samotarati; Skt. caus. ˚tārayati, and ppp. ˚tīrṇa,; goes down, descends (into water): (mahāsamudre) vyavasitāḥ ˚taritum.)

, ger. (of Vedic sam-ava-dhā-, rare and hardly in this mg.; Pali samodahati, hardly in this mg.), setting down (heavily): na sarvakāyaṃ ˚ya, (we will) not (sit down) plunking down the whole body = Tib. lus thams cad kyis ljid gyis mi dbab, we will not throw (or fall) down with the weight of the whole body.

(= AMg. samoṇamai, pple. samoṇamanta,; sam- with Skt. avanamati, Pali onamati), bends down (upon, acc.): samonamantu nabhato jaladharā taṃ = (vs), let clouds bend down from heaven upon it (viz. the grove where the Bodhisattva was about to be born).

, nt. (to next with -ana; = Pali samosaraṇa; late Skt. once, acc. to comm. = nivāsa,), also ˚ṇa-tā (state, condition, of …); written sometimes ˚śaraṇa (which has misled some interpreters into connecting it with Skt. śaraṇa), primarily coming together, gathering, uniting, collection: so regularly Tib. yaṅ dag par ḥdu ba, (sarvadharma-˚ṇasāgara-, sea of gathering of all dharma, cf. below); (see araṇa); (here alternative Tib. gzhol ba, acc. to coming down, also absorption in, besides ḥdu ba); sahālokadhātu-˚ṇāsu (Bhvr.) sarvalokadhātuparaṃparāsu, in all the series of world-systems that are joined with the sahā world-system; (mahāsāgarabhūtaṃ, sc. bodhicittaṃ) sarvaguṇaratna-˚ṇatayā, it is like the great ocean, because it is a gathering of all the jewels of virtues; sarvatraidhātukasvapna-˚ṇajñānena, by knowledge of the collection of dreams which constitute the whole triple universe; since union with something may amount to attainment of it, attainment is often the best English rendering, esp. when a state or condition is what is united with or attained: (dharmavinayo …) nirvāṇa-˚ṇaḥ (Bhvr.), characterized by attainment of nirvāṇa; yāvad eva sattvāḥ sattvadhātau saṃgraha-˚ṇaṃ gacchanti, … arrive at attainment of (or perh. at coming together in) a unity (saṃgraha); dharmadhātu-(q.v.)-˚ṇa-cakraṃ; saptadhana- ˚ṇākāraṃ (sc. śrutaṃ, holy learning) (written ˚śaraṇa, whence wrongly protecting; rather, attaining); (pañca-, so read)-dharmā bodhisattvasya piṭaka- ˚ṇatā (˚śar˚), conditions for acquisition (= learning) of the piṭakas; ˚ṇaṃ saddharmanetrārakṣaṇārthaṃ ye (sc. mantravarāḥ, line 7) sādhayiṣyanti, which will effect attainment (not sécurité,; written ˚śar˚; sc. of religious learning), the goal of which [Page566-b] is the keeping of the Eye of the Good Law; buddhakṣetravyūha-˚ṇa-; two bodhisattva-samādhi are named sarvakṣetrasamanta-˚ṇādhiṣṭhāna, basis of complete attainment of all (Buddha-)fields, and sarvajñānāvartābhimukha-˚ṇa; -praveśa-˚ṇa-, attainment of entrance (or penetration); tathāgatānāṃ kalpapraveśa-˚ṇa-jñānāni, yad uta, (17) ekakalpāsaṃkhyeyakalpa-˚ṇa-tā, and others in ff.

(= Pali samosarati; Jain Skt. in diff. mg.; cf. prec.), primarily comes together, unites, associates: kalpaṃ tābhi sahā samosṛto (associated with them) vihareyaṃ (vs); śrota-samudra mamātiviśuddho yatra samosari śabda-śeṣāḥ (unmetr., read śabda aśeṣāḥ or -viśeṣāḥ?) (vs), … in which all, or various, sounds have gathered together; (dharmaśarīru …) yatra samosari loka aśeṣaḥ (vs); (mārgū,, …) yatra samosarī jina aśeṣā (vs); sarvaguṇālaṃkāra-samavasṛtaṃ divasam, joined (provided) with the ornament of all good qualities; as with samavasaraṇa, sometimes to be rendered get into, attain, usually with acc., once loc.: praṇidhiṃ samavasaran, cited, attaining a solemn vow (‘earnest wish’); etc (sc. dharmāḥ) nītārthe (q.v.; loc.) samavasaranti, they come to (have), attain to, the established meaning (of the word), i.e. it is realized (by the Bodhisattvas) that states of being (dharma) are just what they are declared to be (unsubstantial, etc.); -ṣaḍgati-samavasṛta-; (read) yāvant' anāvaraṇa-satya samosaranti, attain to (comprehension, realization of) the Truths.

, m.(unrecorded; to Skt. samavasṛjati), ˚gaḥ = Tib. rgyun yaṅ dag par bead pa, continuous complete stopping or suppression (in religious sense, like Skt. saṃnyāsa); Chin. also continually stopping or cutting off flow.
(cf. AMg. samohaṇati, in different specialized mg.), destroys, removes, abolishes: ˚hanti; utsṛṣṭaṃ ˚hanti (hanti, without samava-, but v.l. samava-).
(unrecorded; Skt. subst. ˚hāra, collection), collects: ger. samoharitvāna dadanti pānaṃ; ˚haritva 22 (having accumulated, sc. merit).
, n. of a Buddha: Samu-śarīru (n. sg.;) (vs).
, n. of a Buddha: ˚riḥ, n. sg., end of line, (vs); or is Sattvāśayaiḥ to be taken as cpd. with this?

, adj. (āmreḍita of sama; = Pali id.), quite equal or equivalent, exactly alike: sarvadharmāḥ samāḥ sarve samāḥ samasamāḥ sadā (vs); (nāsti me kaścid) āśayena sarvaloke samasamaḥ (fully equal), kutaḥ punar uttara ity …; Siddhārtha-kumārasya na kocit (but mss. kvacit, which may be kept, anywhere) samasamo tathā yuddhe vā …; utsāhenāsya loke ˚mo na bhaviṣyati; (se for asya); na koci (v.l. kvacin, read ˚cit) puruṣo varṇarūpeṇa ˚mo bhaviṣyati; etasya varṇavīryeṇa (v.l. vara˚) loke nāsti samāsamo (ā m.c.) (vs); te rūpeṇa … samasamo na bhaviṣyati; nāsti te ˚maḥ kutottaro (vs); sarvaṃ ˚maṃ bhavati nirviśiṣṭaṃ; ˚mā mātāpitara ācāryopādhyāyāḥ; (na caiṣāṃ) sarvajagati ˚mo 'sti jñānena; indicating a repetition (like peyālam), satkareyā ity etaṃ samasamaṃ, this is just the same (as in line 13, beginning satkareyā); samasamaṃ, adv., at the very same time: Rājagṛhe ˚maṃ … parvaṃ vartati. See next.
, ppp. (to prec. with bhavati), become exactly like (with instr.): (pāṃsunā) ˚tāni (so divide).

, adj. (cf. Pali ˚paka), (food) having curry (sauce) equal (to the rice in amount): na ˚kam (sc. pratigrahīṣyāmaḥ); in the Pali parallels, and, there is no negative, and samasūpakaṃ must be taken to mean having sauce in the right amount, which acc. to the comm. is one quarter of the rice.
, m.,, or ˚kṣarāvakara,, or with ˚kṣarāvakāra, m., n. of a samādhi. In another list,, the reading is ˚kṣarāvakāra as in.
, adj. compv. (cf. āgāḍha-tara), very serious, severe: ˚raṃ duḥkhaṃ.
, ppp. (unrecorded; sam-ā-grah- rare and only Vedic), collected, assembled: ˚ta-puṇyāha-prasthānabhadrāṇāṃ … baṇijāṃ.
, adj. ifc. (Skt. ˚ra plus -in), having, characterized by … conduct: śuklakarma-˚rī (n. sg. m.).
, name, a few times in late Vedic texts, = Pali samaññā; see s.vv. samajñā, samanyā.)

, ppp. (= samādatta, q.v.; to samādiyati, Skt. sam-ā-dā-; = Pali samatta, acc. to and = Skt. samāpta, but this is disproved by collocation with samādinna,, and (vatapadāni) samattāni samādinnāni), adopted, taken upon oneself, esp. of religious and moral obligations: ˚tta-saṃvarasya (see saṃvara); pareṣāṃ cāsamātte (v.l. ˚mādatte) tasmiṃ kuśale samādāpanāya varṇavāditā, samātte (v.l. samādatte) vā punaḥ saṃpraharṣaṇāya; śīlaṃ ˚ttaṃ rakṣati; (bodhisattva-śīla-saṃvara-)-samādānaṃ samāttam; samātta-śīlaḥ (Bhvr.); cintāyāḥ su-samātta-tvāt; daśakuśalakarmapatha-˚ttānāṃ sattvānām (here the ppp. has active force, who have adopted …, see next).

, ppp. (= prec. and Pali, also BHS, samādinna; cf. the following items, and esp. samādāya, samādiyati), adopted, taken on oneself, of a moral or religious course; active in force: pañca śiṣyāpada- (q.v.)samādattā, having adopted the five moral precepts, of Māyā; nāgarājā … upavāsaṃ ˚tto, and mama … upavāsaṃ ˚ttasya 6, having undertaken a fast.
, m. (or adj.; Pali id.; to ˚dapeti; = ˚dāpaka), one who incites (another) to assume or take upon himself: pravrajyā-˚ko … bhūtakalyāṇamitra(ṃ)? (prose!; em. ˚dāpako? cf. next).

(Pali id.; = ˚dāpana, ˚nā; cf. next), incitement to assume, to take on oneself: bodhayi citta-samādapanena (mss. ˚yanena; ed. prints citta as separate word) (vs), by incitement towards thoughts of enlightenment; here ˚dap˚ may be m.c.; but, buddhayāna-˚dapanāṃ na śṛṇvanti is prose; em. to ˚dāpanāṃ, perh. rightly, since samādapeti occurs only in vss; cf. however prec.

(only in vss, perh. m.c.; = Pali id.; cf. prec. two) = ˚dāpayati, q.v., incites, inspires (a person, acc.) to (a goal, when expressed acc. or loc.): pravrajya (acc.) ye cāpi samādapenti; ˚petī (mss. and) bahubodhisattvān acintiye 'nuttami (so read) buddhajñāne; various forms, always with object bahubodhisattvān, no goal expressed,;;;;. Pali (see) uses dat. or loc. of goal; with samādetvā once acc. (and acc. of the person also). See also next.

, prob. only erroneous reading for ˚diyati or ˚dapeti, qq.v.; (1) = ˚diyati, assumes, takes on oneself a religious duty: ˚dayitvā (sc. the moral and religious practices mentioned in the prec. line) [Page567-b] (vs), read ˚diyitvā, to ˚diyati, with same line; in (vs) mss. samodayāmi (prāṇehi ahiṃsa, so read, see v.l., brahmacaryaṃ ca), for which samādayāmi might be read, but properly reads samādiyāmi with same line and; (2) for the caus. samādapeti, ˚dāpeti, qq.v.: saṃbodhimārga (acc.) sada sattva (acc. pl.) ˚dayanti (vs, read ˚dapenti, or possibly ˚dapanti with a for e), they ever incite creatures to take up the way to enlightenment; śīla samādayi (read ˚dapi, prob. aor., possibly ger.) yad bahusattvān (vs), and so, vīrya samādayi (read ˚pi) yad bahusattvān 11 (vs); in (vs) Nep. mss. samādayanto bahubodhisattvān, ˚dapenti, ed. em. ˚dapento; certainly ˚dap˚ is to be read.]

, nt. (once possibly m.; = Pali id.; to samādiyati etc.), (1) assumption, taking upon oneself, undertaking, of any course of action: sarveṣāṃ karmaṇāṃ karma-˚nānāṃ, of all acts and undertakings of acts; -karma-˚na-; sarvakarma-˚na-; rarely of evil courses, (mithyādṛṣṭi-karma-)˚nahetoḥ; mithyādṛṣṭi-˚nāt sattvā gacchanti durgatiṃ (= Pali); oftener of moral or religious undertakings, karmapatha- (q.v.) (mss.); vrata-˚na;; bhagavāṃ … ātmano guṇa-˚naṃ viditvā; śīla-; śīlasaṃvara- (see samātta); kuśala-; dharma-˚neṣu, in the assumption of moral duties (but catvāri dharma-˚nāni include both good and bad programs of behavior); sarvajagac-cittasamādānānantavarṇakāyanirmāṇasamudrameghān (acc., sc. apaśyat), seemingly … characterized by assumption of the mentality of the whole world; cf. (jitvā … rāgadveṣau) citta-˚na-balena, by the power of assumption of (the right) mentality (otherwise); (2) without specific expression of complement, formal undertaking, vow (since under 1 the assumption is usually of a moral or religious duty): eṣa me samādāno (but v.l., better, evaṃ me ˚naṃ), mama maraṇaṃ ihaiva bhaviṣyati, this is my vow, I shall die right here; tena dāni ˚naṃ (below, lines 7, 20, it is called vrata-˚naṃ) kṛtaṃ, na mayā adinnaṃ … paribhoktavyaṃ; tasyāsi (= ˚sīt) ˚naṃ (foll. by quotation of the vow); ˚nam = Tib. yaṅ dag par blaṅs pa, completely taking on oneself, or yi dam, vow; niyojayitāro bodhisattva-˚nena, persons who make one possessed of the vow of bodhisattvas; ˚naṃ kurvanti; ˚nāni … gṛhītāni; askhalita-˚nam (Bhvr., acc. sg. m.), not untrue to his vow; dṛḍha-˚na (both Karmadh. and Bhvr.; = Pali daḷha-˚na,;), a firm vow, or having …,, ˚naḥ, Bhvr., = Tib. yi dam la brtan pa;;;;;;, etc.; (dṛḍhaṃ) ˚nam akarot.
, adj. (to ˚dāna plus -ika), (sc. a religious practice) undertaken as a solemn vow: ˚nikam.

, m. (adj.; to ˚payati; cf. ˚dapaka), one who incites (another) to assume or take to himself; also absolutely, one who inspires (another): tathāgatajñānadarśana-˚paka evāhaṃ (prose), I am just the one who inspires (people) to the sight of Tathāgata-knowledge; catasṛṇāṃ parṣadāṃ … ˚pakaḥ; tathāgatadarśana-˚pakaḥ (prose); ˚pakena bodhisattvena (context indicates reference to assuming the śikṣāpadāni); mss. write ˚dāyaka sometimes, kept by in sarvabodhisattva-˚dāyaka-samuttejaka-saṃpraharṣaka ity ucyate (surely ˚paka must be read, with, see s.v. ˚dāpayati 4); teṣāṃ ˚dāpakaḥ (mss. ˚dāyakaḥ).

(n. act. to ˚dāpayati with ana; see also ˚dapana, ˚nā; also written erroneously ˚dāyana), instigation (of others) to assume, take on themselves, the goal most often preceding in comp.: prāṇātipātavairamaṇya (q.v.)-parasattva-˚panatvād (so read for ˚yanatvād); prativirati-˚panā, also ˚panatā; -kuśalacaryā-˚pana-; sarvasattva-samacitta-˚pana-; parasattva-tathāgatadarśana-˚pana-; -sattva-˚pana-; pravrajyā˚panā; buddhajñāna-˚panatā sarvasattveṣu (instigation towards Buddha-knowledge in reference to all beings, i.e. instigation of them); buddhabimbadarśana-sattva-˚panatayā; tathāgatajñānadarśana-˚pana-hetunimittaṃ sattvānāṃ; without complement, yayā ˚panayā yena kalyāṇamitrasaṃcodanena; ˚panā (comm.); goal in loc. (cf. samādāpayati 2), ˚na, see s.v. samātta; (sattvānāṃ …) samyaksaṃbodhau ˚pana-hetoḥ; arthe ˚panā

(to ˚dāpanā, see prec., plus prob. pejorative -ka, f. -ikā), instigation to religious duty, in para-˚, on the part of others: na para-˚nikayā nāpi paraspardhayā (not because of instigation by others, and not thru rivalry with others) dhīro bodhisattvo veditavyaḥ. (These are unworthy motivations.)

, also (in vss, perh. m.c., but cf. ˚dapaka, ˚dapana, and Pali) ˚dapeti, q.v. (= Pali samādapeti, no ˚dāpeti recorded; primarily caus. to samādiyati in Pali and BHS), (1) causes to assume, to take upon oneself, usually a moral or religious duty: ˚yati = Tib. yaṅ dag par (= sam) ḥdzin (or byed) du ḥjug, cause to take or to do; personal object, if expressed, regularly acc.; impersonal object, that which the personal object is incited to take on himself, may be acc., (bodhisattvayānam eva) ˚yati (prose), (the Buddha) incites to take on the Bodhisattva-vehicle only; but much oftener (2) incites (to), with loc., which seems to imply weakening of the orig. lit. mg.: te codārāyāṃ buddhabodhau ˚pitāḥ; (aśrāddhaṃ … śraddhāsaṃpadi) ˚yati;; dāne cainān ˚yati; parāṃs tatra kuśale ˚yati; mahājanakāyaṃ buddhānusmṛtau ˚paya; this is the regular construction and is very common; sometimes the thing instigated (to) is not a religious or moral duty, as in, (Śakra says to a king: yadi kaścic) cyavanadharmā devaputro bhaviṣyati, tat te putratve ˚payiṣyāmi, … I will instigate him to become your son, and so, (mayā tvaṃ Praṇādasya rājño putratve) ˚pito; , or (v.l.; Tib. mu-khu-li) Samutkhulī (cf. also Utkhalī), n. of one of the four goddesses who attend the Bodhisattva in his motherʼs womb:. See s.v. Sūtkhalin (m.).

, a crossing over (cf. next), in an-a-samuttaro (vs), having no crossing over, that cannot be crossed over, see under an-a-. assumes that ˚tara is for ˚tāra (next), presumably m.c.; meter does indeed require a short penult. But neither ˚tara nor ˚tāra seems to be recorded except here and in the passages, which are substantially repetitions of a single passage.

, m. (cf. Skt. uttāra), a crossing over, of rivers (cf. prec.):; (Vetranadyāṃ tīkṣṇaśastra-)saṃpātayogena ˚raḥ; similarly;; all substantially one passage; nom. sg. ˚tāraḥ except in where ˚tāraṃ of mss. and ed. is prob. an error for ˚tāraḥ.

(cf. uttārayati), the carrying thru to the end: (tatra ca … Sujātā … Bodhisattvasya duṣkaracaryāṃ) carata ādita eva Bodhisattvasya vratatapaḥsamuttāraṇārthaṃ (Tib. brtul zhugs, = vrata, daṅ dkaḥ thub, = tapas, ñams ḥog tu chud par bya ba daṅ) śarīrasyāpy āyatanahetoś ca pratidivasam aṣṭaśataṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ bhojayati sma; the passage is not entirely clear to me in either Skt. or Tib.; interprets uttāraṇa and its Tib. rendering as interruption, departure from; I render: Now Sujātā, from the very beginning of the time when the Bodhisattva was performing austerities, in order to bring the Bodhisattvaʼs vows and penance to a successful conclusion, and also for the sake of support of the body (whose body?), fed every day 800 brahmans. (And she made an earnest wish: ‘Upon eating my food, may the Bodhisattva attain supreme enlightenment’.)
, m. (adj., to next plus -aka), one who inflames, incites:, see samādāpaka;, after samādāpaka, q.v.

(= Pali ˚tejeti; cf. Skt. uttejayati and samuttejana), inflames, incites (to religious courses), regularly in a cliché with samādāpayati, q.v. for references, and other verbs; same cliché with omission of samādāp-, ˚jayitvā;. See prec. and next.
(n. ag. to prec.), one who inflames, incites: (kalyāṇamitrāṇi) … ˚yitāraḥ pratipattiṣu (after samādāpayitar).

, or ˚ika, adj. (or subst.; to Skt. ˚na; cf. Pali Atthasālinī dvi-samuṭṭhāniko, having two causes), (a thing) that causes (or, if Bhvr., is caused by?): (manāpāsecana-)˚nakā, or ˚nikā (so mss.; n. pl. nt.) (prose).
, adj. (cf. Pali samuṭṭhā˚; to Skt. ˚thāpayati plus -aka), arousing, inciting: ˚kaḥ = Tib. kun (text gun, corr. in Tib. Index) nas sloṅ ba po.
, presumably a hollow bowl, = saṃpuṭa, q.v.:, and acc. to.

, m. (rarely nt. in,; = Pali id.; cf. Skt. udaya; see also samodaya), origin: duḥkha-sam˚, origin of misery, the second of the four Noble Truths, see s.v. āryasarya; also used alone, without duḥkha, in the same sense,;;;. See also next.

, m. arising and passing away (of the skandhas): pañcasu upādānaskandheṣu [Page572-a] samudayāstaṃgamān paśyī (in the foll. lines,, samudaya and astaṃgama are used separately). Cf. (Skt.) udaya, and prec.

(= Pali id. in mg. 1; Skt. has not even ud-ā-ga˚), (1) arises, comes into being or sight, appears: saptādityāḥ kalpasaṃvartanyāṃ ˚gamiṣyanti, at the destruction of an age seven suns will appear; (jvaraparidāghanidānāḥ) sarvaśoka … upāyāsāḥ ˚gacchanti, all miseries (etc.) arise; abhivilokanā-pūrvaṃgamehi dharmehi (conditions) samudāgacchamānehi (loc. abs.), as … were arising, appearing; (tasya sarvacittotpāde) daśānāṃ bodhisattvapāramitānāṃ samudāgama-paripūriḥ ˚gacchati; ayam api mahāpṛthivī udakahradaṃ viya ˚gacchet ( ˚gacchati);, this great earth, also, appeared (arose, presented itself, in the beginning of an aeon), as if a pool of water; (2) in there seems likely to be either a drastic abbreviation or a corruption: na cātra śithilena bhavitavyaṃ, na ca śeṣāsu (= śikṣāsu, rules of morality?) na samudāgacchati, and (yet) in this case one must not be lax, and one does not fail to remain (steadfast? or, he does not fail to make a start, to practise?) in the others (? transl. ignores the second negative). See samudāgata (ppp.) and ˚gama(na).

, ppp. (to prec.; cf. Pali id., and next), (1) arisen (after), following upon (in comp.): grīṣme vasanta-˚ta-j(y)eṣṭhamāse (so, as one cpd.) (vs), in summer, in the month Jyaiṣṭha (first summer month), that comes after spring; (2) arrived, attained (at or to a religious goal, esp. enlightenment); may be said of the person who attains the goal, in which case the goal (enlightenment) may be understood from the context and may lack formal expression; or of the goal attained: ˚taḥ = Tib. (as for ˚gamaḥ) yaṅ dag par ḥgrub pa, or ḥthob pa, completely accomplished or attained (gender indicates personal application); anantakalpaiḥ ˚to 'si (vs), after endless ages you (a Buddha) have attained (arrived, sc. at enlightenment, as context shows; not arisen, appeared; Tib. yaṅ dag bsgrubs); (eṣa buddho bhagavāṃ asaṃkhyehi kalpehi) ˚gato arhan samyaksaṃbuddho … (as prec.); prajñāpāramitāyāṃ ˚taḥ; of the goal attained, pūrvajanma-˚takuśalacitta-, good thoughts attained in previous births; dīrghakāla-˚ta-buddhī (vs), having attained (to) buddhi thru a long time (said of a Buddha); sarvabuddhadharma-˚ta-buddheḥ (prose), as prec.

, m. (cf. prec. and Pali id.,, where mg. is not clear), (1) approach (to), arrival (at), attainment (of), a religious goal, esp. enlightenment, which is to be understood when no goal is specifically named: ˚maḥ (for Tib. see s.v. ˚gata); jñātvā ˚maṃ (mss. ˚ma-)saṃbodhau; paramo hi ˚ma īśvarāṇām (vs), attainment (of enlightenment); samyaksaṃbuddhānāṃ ˚maḥ so 'pi lokottaro (prose); the seventh of seven mahattvāni of the mahāyāna (of bodhisattvas), (˚ma-mahattvaṃ saivānuttarā samyaksaṃbodhiḥ; yasyātmabhāva-˚masyānyaḥ ātmabhāva-˚maḥ samo nāsti, kutaḥ punar uttari … ṣaṇ mahattvāni hetubhūtāni ˚gama-mahattvasya; tat punar ekaṃ ˚gama-mahattvaṃ phalasthānīyam eṣāṃ ṣaṇṇāṃ veditavyaṃ);; pratyekabuddhayāna-sam˚; yo 'py ayaṃ … ṣaṭpāramitā-˚mo; pāramitā-sam˚ (also), and see s.v. samudāgacchati; yathā puṇyajñāna-˚gamāya saṃbhavati (prose), so that it results in attainment of …; ye jñāna-pāramitā-caryā-prakāra-pravicaya-praveśa-saṃbhava-˚gamā(ḥ); (2) (vs) samudāgamas tṛṣṇa dukhasya saṃbhavaḥ could be rendered craving is the origin, the source, of misery; no v.l. is cited but em. to samudāgatā on the basis of Chin. renderings, which seem to agree with Tib., sred pa kun ḥbyuṅ las ni sdug bsṅal skye, [Page572-b] app. when craving has arisen, misery arises. But more likely tṛṣṇa, m.c. for tṛṣṇā, is gen. (): the origin of misery is the arising of craving, which accords with Chin. and Tib.
(nt.; = prec.), arrival (at, a stage of religious development), attainment (of it): Dīpamkaro Meghasya … mahā-˚naṃ ca jñātvā kuśalamūlasambhāraṃ ca cetopraṇidhānaṃ jñātvā ….

(once ger. ˚cārya, as if from *˚cārayati; = Pali ˚carati; note that even Skt. uses the noun samudācāra in the mg. address), addresses, speaks to (with acc., once seemingly gen., of person, and usually inst. of the words used): mā yūyaṃ bhikṣavas tathāgatam āyuṣmadvādena samudācariṣṭa (mss. ˚ṣṭaḥ, ˚ṣṭe); (vs) (tān eva dṛṣtva [mss. dṛṣṭa] …) ślakṣṇābhi vāgbhir … samudācaranti; and 9 kumāra(ka)vādena samudācaritavyaṃ manyati, thinks fit to address as ‘boy’; (prose) (mā bhavanto āryasya upālisya) hīnajātyena samudācaratha (the gen. instead of acc. is curious; is it to be taken as dependent on hīnajātyena?); svāgatavādena samudācaritas; mūtrapurīṣavādena samudācaritā(ḥ); (svāgatavādasamudācāreṇa) tāṃ samudācārya (if not a misprint or error, implies ‘caus.’ ˚cārayati; or denom. to samudācāra, in the same sentence?) kathayati; bhikṣuṇyo dāsīvādena samudācīrṇāḥ; āśīviṣavādena samudācaritāḥ.

, m. (mgs. 1 and 2 as in Skt., mg. 3 Skt. Lex.), (1) behavior, manner of conduct (= Skt.); in list of 8 samudācāra of a Bodhisattva in the 1st bhūmi (tyāga, etc.); they resemble roughly the 10 bhūmipariśodhakā dharmāḥ of a Bodhisattva in the 1st bhūmi,; (2) address (= Skt.; see s.v. samudācarati for); in possibly (modes of) address, part of the education of a brahman, see s.v. autkara; (3) intention, purpose: (yadā) hi … asurāṇām evaṃrūpāḥ samudācārā utpatsyante, devāṃs … yodhayiṣyāma iti, etc.; (22) te samudācārāḥ punar evāntardhāsyanti.
(nt.; cf. prec.), performance: punaḥpunaḥ ˚ṇāt, from doing it again and again.
, adj. or subst. (to ˚cāra plus -ika), (matter) of conduct: evaṃrūpasya … kāya-˚kasyāvakāśo na bhavati; see also ā-samud˚.
(to ˚carati, q.v., plus -in), addressing, speaking to: paruṣavacana-˚rī, … with harsh words.

, (nt.) and ˚nā (see; as if n. act. in -ana to *samudānati = ˚neti, ˚nayati; = samudānayana), acquisition, esp. of kuśalamūla: (sarvakuśalamūla-)˚nanāya (prose), Tib. yaṅ dag par sdud pa; ˚nanāyāś ca … kuśalāna mūlāna (vs), Tib. yaṅ dag bsgrub phyir; read sarvakuśalamūlasamudānanāya (text samādānanāya) vīryaṃ (prose), Tib. yaṅ dag par sgrub pa; kuśalamūla-˚nanayā (prob. so, or ˚nanatayā, for text ˚natayā) atṛptatā (prose); ˚nanāyā kuśalasya vīrya(ṃ) (vs), Tib. yaṅ dag sgrub pa; v.l. for ˚nayanāya; in (prose) text asaṅgaprajñā-˚nayana-tayā, but most mss. ˚dānatayā or ˚dānatāyai, prob. read ˚dānanayā or ˚dānanatayā as in (unless these two passages justify assumption of *samudāna = ˚dānana; cf. samudānīya?).

(m.?), also ˚ya-tā (n. act. to ˚nayati; = Pali id., in su-˚nayā, Bhvr., easily acquired or accomplished,; not, of course, gdve. with), (1) acquisition or collection: sarvauṣadha-˚yaṃ ca kartum; vipulapuṇyasaṃbhāra-˚ya-cittā; see under (2) for; (prabhedārthābhiniścayajñānasaṃsārabalaviśeṣa-)˚ya-mahāvyūhaṃ ca nāma dharmamukham; in (vs), text corruptly [Page573-a] ˚nayaṃ prabodhi, see Crit. App., read prob. samudānitāgrabodhiḥ (˚nita- see under ˚nayati), metr. correct; (2) preparation, making ready (a ship; see s.v. samudānayati 5): mahādharma-nau-˚nayatodyuktānāṃ mahādharmaratnapuṇya-˚ya(acquisition, to 1)-kṛtavyavasāyānām.

, rarely ˚te (= Pali samudāneti; see prec. and foll. items; ppp. sometimes ˚nita and ger. ˚niya,; cf.; infra, and see samudānana; note also irregular ˚nīmahe; in text of sam-upā-nī- is often printed while in the same passage has sam-ud-ā-nī, e.g. ˚nīya, cf.; misreading?), (1) gathers, collects: kṣīraṃ … gosahasrād (so with all mss.) … samudānayitvā (vs); (gandhamālyaṃ) ˚nītaṃ; (gandhaṃ, mālyaṃ, puṣpaṃ, cūrṇaṃ) taṃ sarvaṃ samudānayatha; kāṣṭhāni ˚nayata; merchandise, for commerce, paṇyaṃ ˚nayatu, or bhāṇḍaṃ (yad vayaṃ … bhāṇḍaṃ samudānīmahe, that we may assemble …, see Chap. 43, s.v. nī 2);; (2) in part perhaps to (1), but at least in part better rendered provides: mahābhaiṣajyaṃ ˚nayitvā; bhaiṣyajyāni ˚netavyāni, and similarly; ˚nitu … bhaiṣaju (vs), Tib. bsgrubs; (sarvadharmabhaiṣajya-)˚nītaḥ, mahāvaidyarājo, having provided (or collected; ppp. with active mg.) all the medicaments of the Doctrine, he is the great King of Physicians (punctuated badly in text); of food, for invited guests, nānnapānaṃ ˚nayet, should not provide food and drink (after inviting guests); ˚nīya (ger.); distinguished from sajjī-kar-, of food, praṇīta āhāraḥ sajjīkartavyaḥ prabhūtaś caiva ˚nayitavyo, you must make ready elegant food and provide it in abundance; (3) either collects (to 1) or acquires (to 4); mahāpariṣā (acc., so mss.) ˚nayitvā, (the Buddha) having got (or collected) a large assembly (of followers); bhogāḥ (enjoyments) ˚nītāḥ; suvarṇalakṣaḥ ˚nīta(ḥ); (4) acquires: prapañcaiḥ samudānitaṃ (vs; i may be m.c.; not to be em. to ˚nvitaṃ with), acquired by vain fancies; ˚nītaṃ gotraṃ (q.v., 3), acquired (in contrast with prakṛtisthaṃ, innate),, defined 5, yat pūrvakuśalamūlābhyāsāt pratilabdhaṃ; usually with religious ends, esp. enlightenment, as object: ˚niya (read ˚yā m.c.; ger.) jñānam idaṃ anuttaraṃ (vs); bodhiṃ ca ˚nayiṣyati (prose); buddhajñānaṃ ˚nayitavyaṃ (prose); bodhisattvacaryāṃ ˚nayiṣyanti (prose); asaṃkhyeyakalpa … ˚nītām anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhiṃ (prose); (read with Tib. and mostly with vv.ll.) saptāsaṃkhyeyeṣu kalpeṣu ˚nīta-sarvakuśalamūlasya dattasaptavidhadānasya (prose); (read) samudānitāgrabodhiḥ (vs); ˚nitaṃ maitrakṛpābhrajālaṃ (vs); ˚nītva varāgrabodhim (vs); bodhi (acc.) ˚niyā (ger.) (vs; Tib. bsgrubs); bodhibalaṃ ˚nayamānaḥ; buddhadharmān ˚nayati; buddhadharmāḥ ˚nayitavyāḥ; (-paripākaṃ …) ˚nayati; (buddhakṣetrapariśuddhiṃ, ˚tra-māhātmyaṃ, ˚trodāratāṃ) ˚nayan; (maunīndraṃ [pra]vacanaṃ) … ˚nītaṃ; dharma, the Doctrine, is referred to as duṣkaraśata-˚nīta, acquired by hundreds of hardships,;; trikalpāsaṃkhyeya-˚nītāṃ bodhiṃ ˚nīya; valgusvaraṃ ca (read co, m.c., with v.l. and) madhuraṃ pramuñca, ˚nitaṃ kalpa-sahasrakoṭibhiḥ (vs), addressed to a Buddha, whose voice is to proclaim the gospel; puṇyaṃ ˚netvā (em. ˚tvāna, m.c.); (5) prepares, makes ready, a boat (cf. samudānaya 2): maṅgala-potaṃ ˚naya (for an ocean voyage); usually fig., dharma-nau, the boat of the Doctrine, ˚nāvaṃ ˚nayiṣyāmi, Tib. sbyar (which is used of a carriage, ready with harnessed horses) [Page573-b] bar bya ḥo; ˚nāvaṃ samudānayitvanā (vs), Tib. legs par sbyar byas la; ˚niyā dharmanāvaṃ; ˚nāva ˚nayanti (vs); ˚nayitva … śivadharmanāvaṃ (vs), śivadharmanāva ˚nayitāsmi (fut.) (vs); dharmanāva ˚nayaty ayaṃ (vs), cited; mahādharmanau- … -puṇya-samudānīta-mahāsārthavāhasya caturogha-pāra-gāmitā-(so, almost, the best ms., and so Tib.; ˚nā-)-bhiprāyasya, which acc. to Tib. means great entrepreneur (sārthavāha) who by … and merit has made ready (yaṅ dag par bsgrubs pa = samudānīta, with active force) the great boat of Doctrine and purposes to go (with it) to the further shore of the quadruple flood.

, nt. (to ˚nayati plus -ana; cf. ˚dānana), acquisition: ˚nam = Tib. (b)sgrub pa, or sbyar ba; ˚nāya (v.l. ˚dānanāya; ˚dānayaṃ) = Tib. legs par sbyar ba, bsgrub pa, or bsdu (to sdud) pa; (sarva)kuśalamūladharma-˚yana-; mahāyānaguṇa-˚yana-; on see samudānana; sarvabuddhadharma-˚yana-.

, adj., quasi-gdve., perh. by haplology for ˚dānanīya, to *samudānati, from which samudānana, q.v.; or possibly to samudāna (if that stem is to be accepted with readings found in and, s.v. samudānana), plus -īya, cf.; to be acquired (cf. samudānayati 4), in duḥkha-˚nīyā anuttarā (samyak)saṃbodhiḥ;.
(to samudānayati, 2), one who provides, with gen.: (miseries arise as caused by jvara-paridāgha,) teṣāṃ na kaścit ˚netā, and no one provides them.
(= samudāgacchati, q.v.), appears, presents oneself: jinasutāḥ … samudayāntv (a for ā m.c.) iha te 'dya kṛpābalāḥ (vs; cf. āyāntu, 19).
, m. (= Pali id.; to Skt. samudāharati, and cf. next), speaking, conversation; see s.v. antarākathā; anta-sam˚.
, adj. (cf. prec.; to Skt. ˚harati), uttering, speaking:; see s.v. yathāvādi-tathākārin.

, in ālaya-samudita, see s.v. ālaya (2): taking delight in is certainly the mg. It is natural to think of em. to saṃmudita; but the corresp. Pali has in and 13 samudita, and this is a v.l. for saṃmudita of text in another parallel On the other hand, we find in Pali similar triple formulas containing -ārāma, -rata, and -saṃmudita in;;. recognizes samudita, excited (allegedly from sam-ud-i, ‘aroused’), as well as saṃmudita delighted, and cites, without reference, samuditamano (elevated, excited) udaggamano attamano, where the meaning seems clearly rejoiced. I have failed to note saṃmudita in BHS, or any other occurrence of samudita in this sense. Surely one of the two words is an ancient corruption of the other.
, m., (1) n. of a samādhi:;; (2) n. of a maharṣi:.
(see s.v. ˚ghāṭayati), removal, destruction: (anuśayānāṃ …) ananyāryamārga-˚na-tāṃ ca yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti (and the fact that the anu˚ find their abolition in, or by, the peerless Noble Path).
(cf. M. samugghaḍia, defined by opened), freed, in vimati-˚ta, of Buddha; two mss. ˚ghāṭita, see ˚ghāṭayati; cf. samudghāṭin, and samudghāta etc.
, m. (see ˚ghāṭayati), removal, abolition (= ˚ghāta): hetudṛṣṭi-˚ṭo; sarvavāsanānusaṃdhi-˚ṭam (acc.).
(nt.; to Skt. ˚ghāṭayati with -ana), [Page574-a] opening (of a stūpa): mahāratnastūpasya ˚ne (prose).

, removes, abolishes, destroys: kleśānuśayāḥ ˚ṭayitavyāḥ; cf. ˚ghaṭana. Skt. has udghaṭati, opens (intr.), and (sam-)udghāṭayati, opens (trans.); in this meaning BHS ˚ghāṭana; it seems that all the other related words (˚ghaṭana etc. thru ˚ghāṭin) have the mg. appropriate to samudghāta and its sept, which is paralleled in Pali. In BHS, but only here so far as recorded, confusion has occurred between derivs. of (sam-ud-)ghaṭ- and han- (caus.).
(see prec.), remover (of), liberator (from): in Vimati-˚ṭin, (no v.l. in; but ˚ghātī with their ms. Ḱ, and so cites the word, with and); cf. (vimati-)samudghaṭita.

, m. (= Pali samugghāta; see also ˚ghāṭa), removal, abolition, destruction:;; kutsitadarśaneṣu doṣa-˚ta-kuśalāḥ, (Bodhisattvas are) clever in rooting out the errors in reprehensible (heretical) systems; ālaya-˚to (see ālaya 2; same cpd. in Pali ˚gghāto); anuśaya-˚tāya (so read,); sarvamāna-˚taṃ (acc.); (anuśayānāṃ …) atyanta-˚tād.
(nt.; Pkt. samugghāyaṇa = vināśa,), plucking out, rooting out, destruction (= prec.): sarvānuśayaśalya-˚na-tayā (prose).
, ppp. (= Pali samugghā˚; to *samudghātayati, cf. ˚ghāta, ˚ghātana), abolished, got rid of; freed from: sarvamanyanā-˚tasya bodhisattvavimokṣasya; sarvālaya-˚ta-cittatāyai.

, adj.-ppp., app. m.c. for Skt. samudita,, arisen, originated: karma vastu-˚tam; ˚tāḥ (vss). Cf. Pali samuddaya (if correct) = samudaya (), but note also vv.ll. and parallels cited, note; also udraya, uddaya in; the Pali forms need further study.
, or () samuddhanana, rude behavior: nt., = Tib. yoṅs su rgod byed. Cf. uddhānana (uddhanana).
, (1) n. of a Buddhist convert:; (2) n. of another convert, in a vaguely similar story:; (3) n. of a nāga king:.
, m., n. of a region in the south:;.
(fem.), n. of a region (in the south):; (here misprinted ˚votā˚);.
(Skt. only ppp. ˚vṛtta and caus. ˚vartayati), rises, swells (of the sea): ˚tamānasyeva salilanidher (by em.).
(in Skt. only once, and in mg. dive in; but Skt. un-majj- oftener in the mg. of this word), springs forth, dives out: dharaṇīvivarebhyaḥ ˚jjante sma.

(cf. Pkt. samuvahasia, ppp.), ridicule (as subst.); or ˚hāsam, ger. (), ridiculing: (tasyāḥ) ˚hāsam aṅgulīkartum ārabdhaḥ (… tayā … tasyāṅgulyo nipīḍitāḥ), he began to ‘make (motions with his) fingers’ ridiculing her(?).
(m.c. for Skt. samutpā˚, thru MIndic samuppā˚,, cf. Pali samuppajjati etc.), causes (a thought, cittam) to arise, produces: ˚dayetsuḥ (˚dayitsuḥ); ˚danīyam.

(Skt. only ppp. ˚śrita; not noted elsewhere), resorts to (acc.): dṛṣṭīṃ (to heresy) ˚yanti (vs).

, ppp. (cf. Skt. upāhita, bewirkt, hervorgebracht,), app. established, festgesetzt, said of a proposition or statement: yathā … ācāryāṇāṃ svayaṃ ˚hitaṃ (vs), as is established (doctrine) of the teachers themselves; text reads maya = mayā after yatha for mss. yathā; if this is right, as I have established (the doctrine) of the teachers themselves (viz. that the child conceived will become either an emperor or a Buddha). , m., a high number: (first saṃmulaḥ, by error, repeated twice as samula-), cited in as sambala, nt., q.v.; also samulaḥ = Tib. dpag ḥbyams (ḥphyam, ḥjal). Seems to have no correspondent in the list.
(m.; = Pali id., also AMg. ˚lāva), conversation: kathā-˚pena ramati; parivrājikāhi sārdhaṃ ˚paṃ karoti.

, f. ˚ikā, adj. (Pali adj., f. ˚ikā,), (a) well-grounded (charge, accusation), opp. amūlaka: ˚kena kṛtena, etc.; ˚likayā śīlavipattyā etc.
, ppp. (see ūhata; = Pali id.), removed, destroyed: na cāsya rāgānuśayo samūhato; yasya jālinī samūhatā (mss. ˚to) tṛṣṇā; dṛṣṭvā ca rāṣṭrāṇi samūhatāni.

, raises: āśvāsapraśvāsā uparudhvā (mss. [Page575-a] ˚ruddhā) ūrdhvaṃ śīṛṣakapālaṃ vātā praharetsu samūhetsuḥ (v.l. samuttejetsuḥ); I believe this would have to be an anomalous denom. to samūhata, q.v., in the different meaning of raised, which is found also with ūhata, q.v.; or at least, this form, if correct, must have been influenced by that word. But it may be that we should read samūhanetsuḥ, to *samūhanati, on the basis of the Pali parallel vātā muddhānaṃ ūhananti (raise); the version is confused and doubtful, vāyur ūrdh(v)aṃ śiraḥkapālam (mss. ˚lām) upanihanti (v.l. upasaṃharati), and āśvāsapraśvāsā ūrdh(v)aṃ śiraḥkapālam (v.l. ˚lā) upanighnanti (v.l. samuvaghnanti) 3—4; implausibly connects the word with the noun samūha, detaching it from its evident direct object śīrṣakapālaṃ.

(for *samayati, denom. to Skt. sama?), is like, resembles (instr.): sameti so 'ntarikṣeṇa nānātvaṃ nāsya labhyate (vs), it (the Buddhaʼs body) is like space, there is no differentiation found in it; na sameti yad uta nānā-prajñaptyā. , nt., a (prob. corrupt) n. of a medicinal plant: (mss.); see vaṃśarocanā.

(m.? once recorded as nt.), prob. origin; only in vss of and may be m.c. for samudaya, q.v.,, but see samodita: grahā … dṛṣṭajātisamodayā(ḥ); ādau tāvad bhavel liṅgam utpātānāṃ samodayam; nānābhāṣa-˚yā(ḥ); kulayoni-˚yāḥ.
, m. (! so also, n. sg. ˚naḥ; cf. Pali odahana, and BHS anvodahana; to Pali sam-o-dahati, for sam-ava-dadhati = ˚dhāti), completely attentive consideration: ˚naḥ = Tib. legs par rab tu rtogs pa.

, adj.-ppp., prob. originated, arisen, come into being, cf. samudaya and samo˚; only in vss of, where it could be m.c.,, for samudita (which seems to occur in Pali in this mg., tho rarely); but Pali has samodita in prose, once at least in the mg. assembled, united (), which samudita has in Skt.; this mg. would be possible in some of the passages (many of which are obscure and likely to be corrupt; they are here reproduced as printed): karma eṣa sadā vindyād vidhimuktā samoditā; tithayaś ca ˚tā; ulkāṃ liṅgair ebhiḥ ˚tām; yasmin deśe ˚tā; yatra sthite ˚tā; nānānāma-˚tāḥ; yo yasya grahamukhyo vā kṣetrarāśisamoditā; mūlyasiddhiḥ ˚tā; mantratantraṃ ˚tam; teṣu siddhis tridhā yātā triprakārāḥ ˚tāḥ, uttamā madhyamā nīcā ….

(= Pali id., Skt. saṃpad), accomplishment; good luck, fortune, wealth: bodhisattvasya abhiniṣkramaṇa- ˚dā (prose), accomplishment of retirement (n. sg.); same, (prose); paramāye varṇa-˚dāye saṃpannā (prose), blest with highest fortune of aspect; cakravarti-˚dā (prose), fortune of a cakr˚; the rest in vss: durlabhā kṣaṇa-˚dā, hard to find is fortune of moment, i.e. a fortunate or auspicious moment; [Page575-b] te āśaya-˚dāya (instr.) viśuddharūpāya (adj. with prec.) samanvitā bhūt, they were endowed with a rich store of mental disposition that was pure in form (otherwise and); na dānaguṇa-˚dā (so with mss.; acc. sg. or pl.).
, n. of a son of Kunāla and heir presumptive of Aśoka: ˚dī (nom.) nāma; ˚dī r- (i.e. ˚dī or ˚dis), and ˚der (gen.),.
, adj. (Skt. ˚na plus specifying -ka,), that has been acquired: (idaṃ ca loptraṃ) … ˚kam.
, or ˚mṛj- (cf. Skt. parā-mārj-, and saṃparimārjati), wipes off: aśru ˚mṛjya (ger.) (vs; submetrical).

, m. (= Pali id., from Skt. and BHS sāṃparāya; see this), future state, a life after death (cf. abhisaṃparāya): gamanīyo saṃparāyo, one has to go to a future life (i.e. to die);; saṃparāya-sukhito; ˚ya-gurukaḥ; as in Pali often contrasted with dṛṣṭa dharma, = dṛṣṭe (dṛṣṭa-)dharme hitārthaṃ vā saṃparāyasukhāya vā; similarly;;.

, adj. (= Pali id., Skt. sāṃpa˚; cf. saṃparāya), of a life after death: (,), contrasted with dṛṣṭadhārmika. But,, assumes that sāṃpa˚ was read, as in Skt.; is ʼs form a misprint? (cf. Pali samparikantati, and Skt. kṛntati, Epic kartati), splits, or cuts off: (govikartanena gāvīye śīrṣakapālaṃ dāleya …) parikartaye saṃparikartaye; so em., mss. (saṃ) parivarttaye.
(Skt. pari-kāl˚), drives, hunts (birds, towards a snare): (śākuntiko … taṃ mahāntaṃ yūthaṃ) yena te kālapāśā tena ˚kāleti (ʼs em.; mss. ˚kīreti, ˚kīleti).

(Skt. pari-paś-), perceives completely: anityatāṃ ˚śyato (pres. pple.) me (vs).

, (MIndic) ppp. = Skt. saṃparipṛṣṭa, which precedes here, completely questioned: yena pūrvaṃ na saṃparipṛṣṭā bhavatīyaṃ prajñāpāramitā na saṃparipṛcchitā na saṃparipraśnīkṛtā …; also in (vs) prob. read (jñānasya śīghratā) … saṃpariprcchitā (text ˚atā).

, ppp. (to pariveṭheti with sam-), all wrapped up: (taṃ śākhāntikaṃ) vṛkṣaśākhehi ˚taṃ … dṛṣṭvā (line 1 above, ātmānaṃ pariveṣṭayitvā).

, in also samutpuṭaka (presumably = Skt. saṃpuṭa, ˚ṭaka, a hollow bowl or anything of that shape), (1) = Skt. añjali, as gesture of respect: kṛtakara-˚ṭas; cf. saṃpuṭita; (2) in ˚ṭa(ka)jātam, become like a hollow bowl (?), in and passage describing a plucked and withered gourd, to which the Bodhisattvaʼs head after his austerities is compared; the general effect seems to be shrivelled: (tad yathā tiktakālābus taruṇo lūna āmlāno) bhavati saṃmlānaḥ samutpuṭaka-jāta (no v.l. in, but Calc. and ʼs ms. saṃpuṭaka˚) evam eva śira āmlānam abhūt saṃmlānaṃ samutpuṭaka-jātam (no v.l.; supported here by Calc. and ʼs ms.); corresp. (sayyathāpi …) tiktālābu haritacchinnaṃ āmilātaṃ bhavati saṃmilātaṃ saṃpuṭajātaṃ evam eva śīrṣakapālaṃ abhūṣi āmilātaṃ saṃmilātaṃ saṃpuṭajātam, repeated;;, sometimes spelled saṃpuṭaka˚, and mss. often ˚pūṭa˚, ˚ṭā˚; but mg. is not certain; Tib. on (both times) rtsub rtsub por ḥgyur ro (gyur to), becomes (became) very rough; the Pali parallel, (also), has … tittakālābu āmakacchinno vātātapena saṃpuṭito hoti saṃmilāto … me sīsacchavi saṃpuṭitā hoti …; comm. so hi vātātapena saṃphuṭati (v.l. saṃphusati) ceva milāyati ca, with a reading different from the text; (3) dual, in comp. with preceding kapāṭa, the two leaves or panels of a door or gate as forming, when opened, the two sides of a container (‘box’ or double ‘bowl’, as it were): (yathāpi … mahānagaradvāreṣu) mahākapāṭa-saṃpuṭāv argalavimuktau pravisāryate (mss.), as in a great city gate the half-boxes (or bowls, hemispheres, possibly as being slightly concave?) formed of the two great panels, when the bolt is removed, are moved apart.
, denom. pple. (to saṃpuṭa q.v.; perh. cf. Pali saṃpuṭita, cited ibidem), made into the shape of [Page576-b] (a hollow bowl, i.e.) an añjali: hastau ˚tau nityau (vs; in description of a mudrā).

(= Pali saṃpurekkharoti, Skt. puras-k˚), (1) attends: bhikṣugaṇa-˚kṛtaḥ (vs); (Bhagavān … saptabhiś ca nikāyaiḥ) ˚kṛto (prose); (Bhagavantaṃ) ˚kṛtya; (2) displays, employs, manifests: karuṇāṃ ˚kṛtya (ger.); sattvānukampām eva ˚kṛtya (both prose).

, adj., quasi-ppp. of denom. , roars loudly; only after corresp. forms of (Skt.) garjati and pragarjati (subject being world-systems, lokādhātu, on solemn occasions): agarjat prāgarjat saṃprāgarjat; ˚jitaḥ;.

, nt. (see also a-saṃ˚; back-formation from MIndic, = Pali saṃpajañña, for *saṃprajānya from ˚jāna, q.v.), consciousness, intelligence, mindfulness, clearheadedness, circumspection; usually associated or compounded with its near-synonym smṛti (as in Pali with sati): described (following a description of smṛti); cpd. smṛti-saṃ˚;;;;;; closely associated with smṛti,;; in and read smṛtyā saṃprajanyenā 'pramādato yogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ (text has ˚janyetāpra˚); not associated with smṛti, paramasaṃprajanyacāriṇī.

, adj.-pres. pple. (thematization of Skt. ˚jānant), conscious, mindful, thoughtful; for instances see Often follows smṛta, q.v. for a few exx.; so Pali sata saṃpajāna. Also saṃprajāna-(or ˚nan-)mṛṣāvādaḥ etc. (), a deliberate lie, = Pali saṃpajāna-musāvāda.
